clue.text: Put in a box or bag returned by a pressman

indicators.note: returned says the word for a bag is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a sac is a bag or pouch, in biology especially
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual newspaperman

explanation.surface: Something gets packed into a box or bag and handed back by a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SAC into CAS, which sits before ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something encased in a box or holder has been boxed up, so the verb fits as past tense.

clue.text: A high-flier requires space to manoeuvre

definitions.text: A high-flier requires space to manoeuvre

parts.words: A high-flier requires space to manoeuvre
parts.note: a high-flier sounds like an ambitious person needing room, but here it is literally someone flying high, who travels and steers in outer space

explanation.surface: An ambitious achiever needs elbow room to get on.
explanation.definitionFit: A Soviet or Russian astronaut flies higher than anyone and works in outer space.

clue.text: Brown is deeply sanctimonious

annotationWithheld.why: Brown is deeply sanctimonious (5): the only parse is PI (sanctimonious) inside SEA, where 'deeply' must give SEA (deep) and also signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Assiduous dieting may be necessary when about 50

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of dieting and the fifty are mixed up together

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A careful slimmer may need to diet once they reach fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately', but it signals rearranging DIETING with L.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone hardworking and painstakingly careful.

clue.text: New claims the old scientist's made

indicators.note: new suggests the letters of claims the are formed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Fresh claims are what the scientist of yesteryear has produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' tells you to rearrange CLAIMS THE; the definition's 's stands for 'is', joining it to 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval chemists who tried to turn base metal into gold were the forerunners of modern science.

clue.text: A fashion for appearing detached

parts.note: a fashion is a way or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A certain style is chosen to look aloof.
explanation.definitionFit: Being absent or at a distance is being detached from the place.

clue.text: Stock limitation should not restrict traffic

definitions.text: Stock limitation should not restrict traffic

parts.words: Stock limitation should not restrict traffic
parts.note: stock suggests shop goods, but it is livestock: a road barrier of bars over a pit that farm animals will not cross, yet cars drive over freely

explanation.surface: Limits on supplies should not hold up the flow of trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal bars over a shallow pit in a road keep livestock in while letting vehicles pass.

clue.text: Damaging a green causes anger

indicators.note: damaging suggests the letters of a green are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Ruining a golf green makes the groundsman furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' only links the wordplay to the verb 'anger'.
explanation.definitionFit: To infuriate someone is to make them angry, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Snappy devil, a social worker — has to join in!

parts.note: an imp is a small devil

indicators.note: in says the word for joining goes inside the insect

parts.note: an ant is the classic social insect that works in a colony
to tie is to join or fasten together

explanation.surface: An irritable rascal and a welfare officer both insist on taking part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a welfare officer but an insect living in a colony; TIE splits ANT as A-TIE-NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone short-tempered and quick to snap at others lacks patience.

clue.text: Stuff brought by river

explanation.surface: Material carried along by a current.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff is old word for woven cloth, like a rough woollen fabric; the Tweed is a river on the English-Scottish border.

clue.text: Craving for drink — not stiff though

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
something not stiff is flexible or bendy

explanation.surface: Thirsting for alcohol, yet without a stiff measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craving' is the adjective sense, begging humbly.
explanation.definitionFit: A humble petitioner is beseeching, craving a favour.

clue.text: Exercise in the French way is gaining currency elsewhere

indicators.note: in says the exercise goes inside the French street

parts.note: rue is French for a street, a way
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A French fitness trend is catching on abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining currency' reads as becoming popular, but 'currency elsewhere' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The money of India and Pakistan, a foreign unit of cash.

clue.text: Round compass, brightly coloured

parts.note: O is round in shape
compass means scope or extent

explanation.surface: A ring around a compass rose painted in vivid hues.
explanation.definitionFit: A vivid hue between red and yellow, as an adjective.

clue.text: Quietly came down as promised

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
a bird that alighted or landed came down

explanation.surface: Someone softly descended, as agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plighting one's troth is pledging marriage, so the word means pledged.

clue.text: Their youngsters may be champions of course

definitions.text: Their youngsters may be champions of course

parts.words: Their youngsters may be champions of course
parts.note: of course looks like naturally, but it means on the racecourse: these breeding stallions sire foals that may win races

explanation.surface: Their children will naturally become winners.
explanation.definitionFit: Stallions kept for breeding sire foals that can become racing winners.

clue.text: For the presentation of outstanding kitchen sink drama?

definitions.text: For the presentation of outstanding kitchen sink drama?

parts.words: For the presentation of outstanding kitchen sink drama?
parts.note: kitchen suggests the garment worn while cooking, and outstanding means projecting: the part of a theatre stage that juts out beyond the curtain

explanation.surface: Asking where a brilliant gritty domestic play might be put on.
explanation.walkthrough: Kitchen sink drama is the 1950s British genre of gritty domestic plays.
explanation.definitionFit: The section of a stage projecting in front of the proscenium arch, named after the garment.

clue.text: The right way to save, don't forget that!

definitions.text: The right way to save, don't forget that!

parts.words: The right way to save, don't forget that!
parts.note: read as ..., gathering up again is a way of saving, while the whole is an urging to keep something in mind

explanation.surface: A reminder about the proper method of putting money by.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember or call to mind; split, it suggests gathering again.

clue.text: Divine being with sound audience

indicators.note: sound signals that the word is to be said out loud

parts.note: a hearer is one of an audience, a listener

explanation.surface: A god accompanied by a listener with good hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound audience' looks like a healthy crowd, but 'sound' says a listener's word is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of the Greek gods, wife of Zeus, is a goddess.

clue.text: Bond's people finding themselves in a welcome situation

indicators.note: finding themselves in says the people end up inside the greeting

parts.note: to greet is to welcome, so a welcome gives a greet
men is a common word for people

explanation.surface: James Bond's associates happen to be in a friendly spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests the spy, but it is a contract; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a binding arrangement or contract between parties.

clue.text: Succeed with the underworld set

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
to set something is to place or put it

explanation.surface: Doing well along with a crowd of gangsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeed' means take the place of, not do well.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed someone is to supplant or oust them from their position.

clue.text: The right mark

parts.note: the score that shows a correct answer, the checkmark a teacher writes beside it

explanation.surface: The correct grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A checkmark shows an answer is correct.

clue.text: Run and puff — nurse needed!

parts.note: a puff is a promotional piece, an advertisement
to nurse is to minister to, tend

explanation.surface: A breathless jogger badly needs medical attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff' is not breath but a piece of publicity, AD; 'nurse' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To run an organisation is to manage or govern it.

clue.text: See the boss before ten in this workplace

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament
IO looks like the figures 1 and 0, making ten

explanation.surface: Visiting your manager before ten in this office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' is a raised knob, not a manager.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or broadcaster's working room.

clue.text: Doctor laid it on a swelling

indicators.note: doctor means tamper with, so the letters of laid it on are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician applied an ointment to a lump.
explanation.definitionFit: Widening or enlargement of an opening or vessel is an expansion.

clue.text: Fed-up with hesitation expressed — put off

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation spoken

explanation.surface: Annoyed by the stalling, someone postpones things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fed-up' reads as annoyed, but 'up' reverses FED to DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: To postpone is to delay till later.

clue.text: A parking complaint made by an American

parts.note: P is the sign for parking
an ache is a minor ailment

explanation.surface: A grumble about parking voiced by someone from the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Native American people of the Southwest.

clue.text: The source of many a benefit

definitions.text: The source of many a benefit

parts.words: The source of many a benefit
parts.note: a benefit is also a fund-raising event, many of which are held in support of a charity aim

explanation.surface: Where many advantages come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason or origin of something, and also a charitable aim that benefit concerts support.

clue.text: Monster duck, almost entirely grey

parts.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket, the shape O

indicators.note: almost entirely says the word grey loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A monstrous duck is almost all grey.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nothing in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eating giant of fairy tales is a monster.

clue.text: If sent back to finish he can be very spiteful

indicators.note: sent back says the letters of if are written backwards

parts.note: a finish is an end

explanation.surface: If he gets returned to the end, he will be vindictive.
explanation.definitionFit: A devil or malicious person is cruel and spiteful.

clue.text: Personal subscription

parts.note: subscription is literally writing underneath; one's own name written at the foot of a document

explanation.surface: An individual membership fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Signing your name at the bottom of a letter is subscribing it in person.

clue.text: Sour, terse characters turned up

indicators.note: characters means the letters of sour and terse are treated as loose pieces to be reordered

explanation.surface: Grumpy, curt people with their noses in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' describes a nose; it is the definition, not an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A French word for a nose that tilts upward at the tip.

clue.text: Choice offered by some, but only some, lecturers

indicators.note: offered by says the letters are provided within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Options given by a few, but only a few, university teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but only some' warns that just part of the words are used: the end of 'some' and start of 'lecturers'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, chosen or select, the pick of a group.
